title: Organizational Sprint Staircase — 60-Day Ops Playbook (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational playbook to align Redwood Inference leadership and teams on a time-boxed, 60-day staircase approach for company priorities, the pre-reads and run-of-show for the all-hands, and an exec update brief we can ship to the board. Draft v0.1: working notes and asks; please comment inline.

Background / context:
- Signals: usage growth in hosted API, increased inbound interest for Dedicated contracts, a handful of regressions in latency SLOs after last deploy, and tighter cash discipline for the next two quarters.
- Goal of this playbook: create a focused, executable plan that ties top-level OKRs to concrete deliverables and comms so teams can prioritize the next 60 days without re-scoping every week.

Top-level company objectives (draft) — 60-day window focus:
1) Objective A: Stabilize and reduce latency tail to meet 99th percentile SLOs for hosted API
   - KR A1: Reduce 99p response latency for text-generation from 620ms to <=420ms for p95 traffic mix
   - KR A2: Reduce production error-rate from 0.8% to <=0.25% (post-retry)
   - KR A3: Ship a hotfix and rollout plan (canary -> full) for the runtime mitigation by Day 18

2) Objective B: Improve unit economics on high-volume embeddings customers
   - KR B1: Identify top 5 embedding workloads responsible for 60% of tokens and map batching opportunities by Day 10
   - KR B2: Deliver quantization profile experiments and a recommendation (A/B) with expected cost delta for top 2 workloads by Day 40
   - KR B3: Pilot caching layer for embeddings with one key customer and validate 20% cost reduction by Day 60

3) Objective C: Increase enterprise pipeline health and enable 2 Dedicated contracts to go to legal
   - KR C1: Convert 2 proof-of-concept Dedicated deals to signed term sheets by Day 60
   - KR C2: Harden Private deployment onboarding checklist and reduce time-to-first-inference for customers from 8 weeks to <=4 weeks
   - KR C3: Publish support SLA playbook for Dedicated by Day 50

60-day staircase (three waves, ~20 days each):
- Wave 1 (Days 0–20): Stabilize & unblock
  - Focus: triage latency regressions, ship hotfix, quick batching wins, all-hands to set cadence
  - Concrete deliverables: runtime hotfix patch, rollback/fallback runbook, top-5 embedding workload list, enterprise pipeline intake review
  - Owners: Serving runtime (hotfix) = Theo Park; Platform/instrumentation (metrics) = Priya Singh; Sales ops (pipeline intake) = Noah Rivera

- Wave 2 (Days 21–40): Scale experiments & cadence
  - Focus: run quantization experiments, pilot caching for embeddings, begin Dedicated deal conversions, internal eval harness for latency testing
  - Deliverables: quantization experiment report, caching pilot onboarding doc, Dedicated legal intake checklist, pre-read for exec update
  - Owners: Applied ML = Priya Singh; Dedicated Sales = Noah Rivera; Release eng = (lead tbd)

- Wave 3 (Days 41–60): Harden & convert
  - Focus: finalize recommendations, run canaries across customer groups, ship support SLA playbook, finalize slide pack for board/exec
  - Deliverables: decision memo on quantization rollout, canary results dashboard, two signed term sheets or clearly documented blockers
  - Owners: Product + Sales for conversion, SRE for SLA playbook

All-hands (week 2) — pre-read & run-of-show (compact):
- Pre-read (sent 48 hours before): 1-page status on each objective (one paragraph + topline KR progress), explicit asks/decisions we want from leadership; 2 dashboards: latency trend + pipeline conversion funnel
- Run-of-show (60 minutes):
  1) 5m — CEO framing: why the 60-day staircase and what success looks like
  2) 10m — Stabilization highlights (runtime hotfix, immediate customer impact)
  3) 10m — Cost & embeddings update with top experiment hypothesis
  4) 10m — Enterprise pipeline and Dedicated update (asks for cross-functional support)
  5) 15m — Breakout Q&A (teams grouped by objective) — capture decisions in live doc
  6) 10m — Closing + immediate next steps + townline owners and timeline
- Moderator: Maya Chen; pre-reads collated by Noah Rivera

Exec update brief (one-pager for execs / board slide bullets):
- Situation: Last week’s deploy introduced a kernel scheduling change; p99 latency regressed. We targeted a hotfix and have a canary running (expected full rollout Day 18).
- Impact: 0.8% error-rate, 4 customer-reported slow requests in prior week, 3 mid-stage Dedicated deals pending additional info on onboarding time.
- Ask: Approve temporary burst budget of 15% capacity for two weeks to run canaries and customer trials; endorse prioritization of runtime hotfix and top-5 embedding batching experiments.
- Metrics to watch: 99p latency, request error-rate, token unit cost for top embedding customers, pipeline conversion rate (POC -> legal)

Decision log (initial items to confirm in first 10 days):
- D1: Approve short-term capacity burst (owner: CFO contact — assigned to James Alvarez) — decision required by Day 4
- D2: Accept quantization pilot for two high-volume workloads (owner: Applied ML) — decision by Day 21
- D3: Sign-off on Dedicated onboarding checklist (owner: Legal + Solutions Eng) — decision by Day 30

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hotfix introduces secondary regressions in less-common models; Mitigation: canary across tiered traffic, automatic fallback to previous kernel variant, dedicated rollback plan
- Risk: Quantization impacts output quality for LLMs in specific prompt families; Mitigation: prompt-preserving evaluation harness + human spot checks and rollback threshold tied to eval scores
- Risk: Sales pipeline stalls on onboarding complexity; Mitigation: create an express onboarding path (two-week pilot template) and assign Solutions Eng shadow resource for each Priority account

Comms and escalation plan:
- CEO/Exec cadence: Weekly 15-minute sync (Mon 9:00) for topline KR status (owner: Maya Chen compiles)
- Alerts: If p99 latency > 800ms for 2 consecutive hours, SRE on-call to page runtime lead + Product PM; status posted to #ops-alerts
- Board notice: Minimal — only if latency issue persists >72h or if a Dedicated contract conversion is delayed beyond Day 60

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- A1: Theo to publish hotfix branch and initial canary plan — due Day 3
- A2: Priya to deliver top-5 embedding workloads analysis — due Day 5
- A3: Noah to assemble enterprise pipeline review doc with 6 priority accounts — due Day 6
- A4: Maya to draft 1-page pre-read and distribute 48h before all-hands — due Day 10

Open questions / things to decide quickly:
- Q1: What is approved temporary burst capacity budget? (Finance/CEO)
- Q2: Who signs as Dedicated legal approver for time-boxed onboarding exceptions?
- Q3: Is the quantization experiment permitted on production traffic beyond canary (guardrails)?

Notes to reviewers (meta):
- This is intentionally compact: we want a single cadence and a small set of measurable deliverables.
- Please leave comments in the doc (inline) or in the linked Confluence canvas if the change requires re-prioritization across quarters.
- If you are the owner for any action item above and cannot hit the due date, flag immediately in #ops and propose an alternate owner.

Appendix (supporting artifacts to attach before v0.2):
- Latency heatmap (by model & seq len) — instrumentation team
- Embeddings token-cost breakdown by customer — finance
- Dedicated onboarding checklist draft — Solutions Eng + Legal

End of draft v0.1 — please comment by EOD Week 1 (two business days after distribution).
